_comment: Claude Code MCP config for the Gaffer factory: the two data-plane MCP servers the agent delivers through. tick.sh renders a runtime copy, substituting __GAFFER_DATA__/dispatch.sqlite/__GAFFER_DATA__/memory.sqlite (runtime DB copies), /opt/gaffer-fixture/dispatch-mcp/bin.js//opt/gaffer-fixture/memory-mcp/bin.js (the built dist bins), and __CLAIM_TOKEN__ (RUNNER-OWNED-BOOKKEEPING: the runner-held delivery claim token, so the agent's token-gated evidence writes resolve it from the server env — the agent never handles the token) and GAFFER_SCOPE_TICKET (the ticket number this mount is bound to — delivery, resume, bootstrap and clarify pass it, every other mount passes it empty — so the dispatch server refuses the agent's writes on any other ticket). The memory server additionally gets GAFFER_FACTORY=1 + fixture-app (the ticket's in-scope repo names) so its DIRECT-APPLY writes (digest / feature) are bound to the ticket's repo scope, fail-closed, plus GAFFER_RECALL_TICKET (the delivery ticket ref) so its READ path can attribute a retrieval to a ticket for memory ROI (empty ⇒ inert, no logging), and GAFFER_REPO_CANONICALS (a JSON object: each ticket repo name → the canonical its file cards are keyed under, so the card tools find them from a worktree; empty ⇒ the agent passes repoCanonical itself). MEMORY_AUTO_APPROVE is pinned to 0 for this agent-mounted server: lore an agent suggests over MCP always lands as a DRAFT for a human, whatever the operator's memory auto-approve setting (that setting covers the runner's own memory writes only). Build the workspace first: pnpm -r build.
